hero.tagline: Copy, move, sync and verify your files, byte for byte.
hero.sub: A desktop file copier for Windows, macOS and Linux, with checksum verification, resume after a crash, two-way sync, undo and its own file server. No account, no telemetry and no AI.
notice.price: Freally File Manager is free today, but it might not be free forever: future versions may be sold.
hero.noDownloads: There are no downloads on this site yet, and the source code is private.
what.title: What it is
what.p1: Copying a big folder with your system's own copy dialog tells you very little: no checksum, no say in what happens to files that already exist, and no way back when the power goes out halfway through.
what.p2: Freally File Manager is a copier built to be trusted with that job. Drop files on its window, pick a destination, and it copies them through your system's fastest copy path. Switch on verification and it reads every copy back and checks it against the original's checksum.
what.p3: Around the copier is everything you reach for afterwards: a history of every job with re-runs and undo, checksum tools, two-way sync and live mirroring, snapshots, a built-in file server and a command line for scripts.
features.title: What is in it
features.copy.title: Byte-exact copies
features.copy.body: Every file is copied byte for byte through your system's own fast paths, and cloned instantly on drives that support it. Pause, resume or cancel any job, and decide before it starts what happens when a file already exists.
features.verify.title: Verified when you ask
features.verify.body: Switch on verification and each copy is read back and checked against the original with one of eight checksums, from CRC32 and xxHash3 to SHA-256 and BLAKE3. A mismatch is reported, never hidden.
features.resume.title: It survives a power cut
features.resume.body: A journal records how far each copy got. After a crash or a reboot, the part already written is checked and the copy carries on from there instead of starting again.
features.sync.title: Two-way sync
features.sync.body: Keep two folders in step in both directions, or mirror one onto the other. A file changed on both sides is a conflict: both versions are kept and you choose.
features.history.title: History and undo
features.history.body: Every job is recorded. Run it again, retry only the files that failed, or undo the last copy or move: undone copies go to the Recycle Bin or Trash, never straight to deletion.
features.checks.title: Check your files any time
features.checks.body: Hash any file with eight checksums, make and check .sha256 or .sfv files, compare a folder with its copy months later, and export a signed report of what was copied.
features.server.title: Your own file server
features.server.body: Serve a folder to other computers over WebDAV, plain HTTP, an S3-compatible API or SFTP, read-only if you like, behind a password or a token.
features.free.title: Free, private, no AI
features.free.body: No account, no telemetry and no machine learning. Your files go only where you send them, and the daily update check can be switched off.
ladder.title: The road to 1.0
ladder.intro: One line per version, oldest first. Every one of them is done: built, tested and tagged.
ladder.rung.v0.19.84: The first release: byte-exact copies with optional verification, resume after a crash, history, two-way sync and live mirror, the file server and the command line, in 18 languages.
ladder.rung.v0.19.85: The Library: deduplicated snapshots you can back up, compare and restore, and repositories you can bring in from or export to restic, Borg and Kopia.
ladder.rung.v0.20.0: Safety nets: undo the last copy or move, delete to the Recycle Bin or Trash, retry only the files that failed, checksum files, and eject a drive when a job is done.
ladder.rung.v0.22.0: Hashing, reports and scheduling: a hash inspector, signed copy reports, re-verify, damaged-media salvage, schedules, favourites, portable mode and accessibility.
ladder.rung.v1.0.0: The correctness release: a full review of the code, section by section, and every fix that came out of it.
ladder.note: A version that is done is built and tagged. None of them is a download on this site: there are no downloads here yet.
honest.title: The things most sites put at the bottom
honest.verify.title: Verification is off until you switch it on
honest.verify.body: Checking a copy means reading it a second time, so it is a setting rather than the default. Choose a checksum in Settings → Transfer, and every copy after that is checked.
honest.notYet.title: Two things 1.0 cannot do yet
honest.notYet.body: It cannot securely shred files, and it cannot copy to cloud storage. Settings already has a place for both, but neither is wired up in version 1.0.0.
honest.network.title: When it goes online
honest.network.body: Copying between your own drives, verifying and deleting make no network requests. It goes online for what you set up, such as the file server or testing a cloud account, and to check for updates when it starts, at most once a day, which you can switch off in Settings → Updates.
honest.downloads.title: There are no downloads here yet
honest.downloads.body: No installer, no preview build and no download link on this site. When that changes, this page will say so.

footer.yours: The files you copy, sync and serve stay yours. Freally File Manager's author claims no ownership of them.
featuresPage.title: Everything it does
featuresPage.lead: A byte-exact file copier with verification, resume after a crash, sync, undo and its own file server, and a record of every job it has ever run.
featuresPage.version: This page describes Freally File Manager version 1.0.0, the current version: everything on it is in 1.0.0.
featuresPage.numbers.title: By the numbers
featuresPage.numbers.intro: Each figure is counted from version 1.0.0's own code. Nothing is rounded up.
featuresPage.numbers.hashes: checksums to verify a copy with
featuresPage.numbers.collisions: choices for a file that already exists
featuresPage.numbers.sidecars: checksum-file formats it writes and checks
featuresPage.numbers.server: ways to serve a folder: WebDAV, HTTP, S3 and SFTP
featuresPage.numbers.systems: operating systems: Windows, macOS and Linux
featuresPage.free.title: Free today
featuresPage.free.body: Everything Freally File Manager does today is free, for everyone: no paid tier, no subscription, no licence key and no account.
featuresPage.cards.title: What version 1.0 does
featuresPage.cards.copy.title: The copy engine
featuresPage.cards.copy.body: Byte-exact copies through each system's fastest path, with instant clones on file systems that support them. Huge folders stream through without filling memory, and you choose before a copy starts what happens to files that already exist: keep both, skip, overwrite, overwrite if newer, overwrite only if different, or ask.
featuresPage.cards.verify.title: Verify after copy
featuresPage.cards.verify.body: Eight checksums: CRC32, MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-512, xxHash3-64, xxHash3-128 and BLAKE3. Each copy is read back and compared with the original, and a mismatch fails the file instead of passing unnoticed.
featuresPage.cards.checks.title: Hash, re-verify and checksum files
featuresPage.cards.checks.body: The Hash panel checks files against a checksum you paste. Re-verify compares a folder with its copy months later without writing a byte. Make .md5, .sha1, .sha256, .sha512, .b3 or .sfv files for a whole folder, and drop one on the window to check it.
featuresPage.cards.resume.title: Crash and reboot resume
featuresPage.cards.resume.body: A journal records each copy's progress. On the next launch the part already written is checked against its hash, and the copy continues from there.
featuresPage.cards.history.title: History, re-runs and undo
featuresPage.cards.history.body: Every job is recorded. Run any of them again, retry only the files that failed, export a signed report, or undo the last copy or move: undone copies go to the Recycle Bin or Trash, never straight to deletion.
featuresPage.cards.sync.title: Sync and live mirror
featuresPage.cards.sync.body: Two-way sync, a mirror in either direction, or contribute-only, with conflicts kept as two files for you to choose between. A live mirror watches a folder and syncs every change you save.
featuresPage.cards.server.title: A built-in file server
featuresPage.cards.server.body: Serve any folder over WebDAV, HTTP, an S3-compatible API or SFTP, from Settings or the freally serve command, read-only if you like, behind a token or a password, with a Prometheus metrics endpoint.
featuresPage.cards.library.title: Snapshots and backups
featuresPage.cards.library.body: A deduplicating repository stores each version of a file once. Browse the timeline, restore any snapshot, back up chosen folders on demand, and bring in repositories from restic, Borg or Kopia.
featuresPage.cards.salvage.title: Rescue a failing disk
featuresPage.cards.salvage.body: Salvage copies whatever can still be read of a file on a failing drive, fills the unreadable spots with zeros so the rest keeps its place, keeps a map of the gaps, and retries only those gaps on a later run.
featuresPage.cards.metadata.title: Nothing quietly lost
featuresPage.cards.metadata.body: Sparse files stay sparse, and alternate data streams, extended attributes and the downloaded-from-the-internet mark travel with each file. A file locked by another program on Windows can be copied from a snapshot.
featuresPage.cards.desktop.title: Part of your desktop
featuresPage.cards.desktop.body: Copy and move from the right-click menu in Explorer, Finder, Nautilus, Dolphin and Thunar, paste through it from anywhere with Ctrl+Shift+V, and schedule saved jobs in your system's own scheduler.
featuresPage.cards.cli.title: A command line for scripts
featuresPage.cards.cli.body: The freally command copies, moves and verifies, plans a job before running it, serves folders and imports backups, and reports in JSON lines with documented exit codes.
featuresPage.speed.title: How fast it is
featuresPage.speed.intro: Measured on 30 April 2026 on one Windows 11 laptop (Intel Core i9-13900HX, 32 GB of memory, a PCIe 4.0 NVMe drive), copying within the same NTFS drive. Each figure is the median of several runs, in MiB per second: higher is faster.
featuresPage.speed.mixed: A folder of 100 files, 100 KB to 150 MB
featuresPage.speed.result: It was the fastest on the folder of files and on the 512 MB file, and a little slower than Robocopy and the Windows copy command on the 256 MB and 10 GB files. It was faster than FastCopy and TeraCopy in every test.
featuresPage.speed.caveat: One machine and one drive, measured with a build from before 1.0.0, and each tool run from its own command line, start-up included. Your numbers will differ, and when the destination drive is the slowest part, every tool runs at its speed.
featuresPage.compare.title: Side by side with the commercial tools
featuresPage.compare.intro: Freally File Manager 1.0.0 next to six commercial tools people buy to copy, check, sync and manage their files. Every cell for another product comes from its maker's own pages, checked on 2 October 2026, and prices are US list prices as of October 2026.
featuresPage.compare.note.perYear: a year, up to five devices
featuresPage.compare.row.verify: Checks each copy against a checksum
featuresPage.compare.note.checksumTool: a checksum tool, not after each copy
featuresPage.compare.row.resume: Resumes a copy after a crash or a reboot
featuresPage.compare.note.afterStop: after a stop, by reopening the list
featuresPage.compare.row.sync: Two-way sync that keeps both sides of a conflict
featuresPage.compare.row.server: Serves a folder over WebDAV, S3 or SFTP
featuresPage.compare.row.undo: Undoes a finished copy or move
featuresPage.compare.row.salvage: Rescues what can still be read from a failing drive
featuresPage.compare.row.report: Exports a report of each file's checksum
featuresPage.compare.summary: The short version: only Freally File Manager has all of it. None of the six lists a server for WebDAV, S3 or SFTP, or a way to rescue files from a failing drive, on its maker's own pages, and of the six only GoodSync documents detecting a sync conflict.
featuresPage.compare.theyWin: Where they win: Directory Opus, Total Commander and ForkLift let you browse and organise all your folders in their own windows, while Freally File Manager 1.0.0 works on the files you hand it. TeraCopy and Directory Opus can securely delete files, and ForkLift, Beyond Compare and GoodSync copy to cloud storage; Freally File Manager 1.0.0 does neither. TeraCopy also offers more checksums: 17 against eight.
featuresPage.compare.asOf: Freally File Manager's column is version 1.0.0, and its price is today's: it is free today, and future versions may be sold. The other products change too; this table is as of 2 October 2026.
featuresPage.why.title: Why it is built the way it is
featuresPage.why.exact.title: Byte for byte, or a failure
featuresPage.why.exact.body: A copy is the same bytes as the original, or it is reported as a failure. And a file that changes while it is being read is flagged, copied again or failed, as you choose, rather than passed off as a clean copy.
featuresPage.why.native.title: The system's own fast paths
featuresPage.why.native.body: It asks Windows, macOS and Linux to copy each file the fastest way they know, and clones files instantly where the file system allows, instead of pushing every byte through a loop of its own.
featuresPage.why.safe.title: Nothing destructive by accident
featuresPage.why.safe.body: A move deletes the original only after the copy has succeeded, undo sends files to the Recycle Bin or Trash rather than deleting them, and undo never touches a file that has changed since it was copied.
featuresPage.why.local.title: It stays on your machine
featuresPage.why.local.body: No telemetry and no account. Your files go only where you send them, and telemetry cannot even be switched on by editing the settings file.
featuresPage.why.noAi.title: No AI
featuresPage.why.noAi.body: Everything it decides comes from ordinary, predictable code: checksums, sizes and timestamps. There is no machine-learning library in it.
featuresPage.limits.title: What 1.0 does not do
featuresPage.limits.verify: It does not verify a copy until you switch verification on in Settings → Transfer.
featuresPage.limits.queue: Jobs cannot be reordered in the queue: each one starts as soon as it is added.
featuresPage.limits.portable: Portable mode keeps settings and profiles beside the app, but history, the resume journal and saved cloud passwords stay on the computer it runs on.
featuresPage.limits.shred: It cannot securely shred files: Settings → Secure delete is there, but nothing in 1.0.0 deletes through it.
featuresPage.limits.cloud: It cannot copy to cloud storage: you can add and test cloud accounts in Settings → Remotes, but no copy goes to them yet.
featuresPage.limits.downloads: There are no downloads on this site yet, and none on this page.

docs.start.p1: Freally File Manager is a desktop app for Windows 11, macOS 12 or later, and Linux. The first time it opens it shows its licence agreement: scroll to the end, then choose I Agree to start, or Decline & Quit.
docs.start.p2: The window is a drop zone above the Activity panel. Add files, Add folders and Import list sit in the header. The footer holds Totals, History, Hash, Re-verify, Salvage, Sync, Library, Tasks and the gear that opens Settings.
docs.start.p3: There are no downloads on this site yet.
docs.copy.s1: Drag files or folders onto the window, or click Add files or Add folders in the header.
docs.copy.s2: The Transfer dropped items dialog opens. Leave Operation on Copy and click Pick destination to choose the folder to copy into.
docs.copy.s3: Under If a file already exists, choose what happens to files that are already there: keep both, skip, overwrite, overwrite only if newer, overwrite only if the content differs, skip if identical and ask otherwise, or ask every time.
docs.copy.s4: Use Order to sort the list by name or size, or drag the rows. Files always come before folders.
docs.copy.s5: Click Start copying. Each file gets a row in the Activity panel with its progress, speed and time left, and the header shows the totals.
docs.copy.p1: To pause a job, focus its row and press Space, or right-click it and choose Pause; Resume carries on and Cancel stops it. Pause all jobs, Resume all jobs and Cancel all jobs are in the header.
docs.copy.p2: If the destination has no room for everything, you are warned before the first byte moves and can pick which items to copy. The dialog also flags names the destination cannot hold, such as reserved names, characters it does not allow and paths that are too long, and offers to rename them.
docs.copy.p3: Use When done at the bottom of the window to close the app, log off, shut down or sleep when every job has finished.
docs.move.p1: Moving works like copying: in the Transfer dropped items dialog, set Operation to Move, pick a destination and click Start moving.
docs.move.p2: Each file is copied first, and the original is deleted only after the copy has succeeded. If anything fails, the original stays where it was and the row is marked as failed.
docs.move.p3: To make every move recoverable, switch on Send moved source files to Trash in Settings → Secure delete: the originals then go to the Recycle Bin or Trash instead of being deleted.
docs.verify.p1: Verification is off until you switch it on. Open Settings → Transfer and choose a checksum under Verify after copy: xxHash3 is the fastest, BLAKE3 is strong and still fast, and SHA-256 matches most other tools.
docs.verify.p2: From then on every copy is checked. The original is hashed while it is read, so it is not read twice; once the copy is written, the copy is hashed too and the two are compared.
docs.verify.p3: A match finishes the row as done. A mismatch fails the row and shows the expected and the actual checksum. If a large copy seems to sit at 100%, the header probably says Verifying: the check is still running.
docs.history.p1: Click History in the footer. Every job is listed with its kind, source, destination, size, status and duration, and you can filter the list by kind, status or text. Export CSV saves it.
docs.history.p2: From a job you can Re-run it, use Retry failed to copy only the files that failed, Export failed to save that list, Re-verify it, or export a Certificate: a printable HTML, CSV or JSON report of every file's checksum, size and status, which you can sign with your own key.
docs.history.p3: Undo, or Ctrl+Z, reverses the newest copy or move after showing exactly what it will touch. Copied files go to the Recycle Bin or Trash, and only if they still match what was copied; moved files go back where they came from.
docs.history.p4: Totals, also in the footer, shows lifetime figures for bytes, files and jobs, and a chart of the last 30 days.
docs.checks.p1: Hash, in the footer, opens the hash inspector. Add files or folders, choose an algorithm and click Hash. Paste a checksum, a line from a checksum file or an SFV row to compare against it, or pick two files to see whether they are identical.
docs.checks.p2: Re-verify, also in the footer, compares a folder with its copy again, at any time and without writing anything. It reports every file that matches, differs, is missing from the copy, exists only in the copy, or cannot be read.
docs.checks.p3: To make a checksum file for a whole folder, right-click a finished job and choose Create checksums (SHA-256). To check one, drop a .md5, .sha1, .sha256, .sha512, .b3 or .sfv file on the window: every file it lists is hashed and the result is shown.
docs.sync.s1: Click Sync in the footer, then Add pair.
docs.sync.s2: Give the pair a label, choose the left and the right folder, and pick a mode: Two-way; Mirror, left to right or right to left; or Contribute, which copies left to right and never deletes.
docs.sync.s3: Click Save pair, then Run now.
docs.sync.p1: When a file has changed on both sides since the last run, nothing is overwritten: the other version is kept beside it as a sync-conflict file, and View conflicts lets you keep the left one, the right one or both.
docs.sync.p2: Start live mirror watches the left folder and syncs again after every change you save. The pair shows Watching while it runs; Stop live mirror ends it.
docs.filters.p1: Settings → Filters applies to every copy: patterns to include or exclude, such as **/*.log or **/node_modules, size and date limits, and whether to skip hidden, system or read-only files. A folder that matches an exclude pattern is skipped whole.
docs.filters.p2: To copy an exact list of files, click Import list in the header and choose a TXT, CSV or JSON file of paths. Copy them flat into one folder, or keep their folders below a common root.
docs.filters.p3: Before a big copy, Export plan in the Transfer dropped items dialog saves a report of what the copy will add, replace, skip or find in conflict, before a single byte moves.
docs.shell.p1: Freally File Manager can add Copy with Freally File Manager and Move with Freally File Manager to the right-click menu: in Explorer on Windows, in Finder on macOS, and in Nautilus, Dolphin and Thunar on Linux. On Windows, Settings → Shell turns them on or off.
docs.shell.p2: Copy files as usual with Ctrl+C (Cmd+C on a Mac), then press Ctrl+Shift+V (Cmd+Shift+V on a Mac) anywhere: the files open in Freally File Manager's dialog. Change the shortcut or switch it off in Settings → General.
docs.shell.p3: On Windows you can go further: Intercept default copy handler, in Settings → Shell, routes Explorer's own copy and paste through Freally File Manager, and each paste then asks whether you want a plain system copy or a verified one. Revert to Windows copy handler undoes it in one click.
docs.library.p1: Library, in the footer, opens the repository: each file's contents are stored once, in deduplicated chunks, and every snapshot is shown on one timeline. The header shows how much is stored on disk against how much it represents.
docs.library.p2: On Sources, add a folder and click Back up now to take a snapshot; a second backup of an unchanged folder takes almost no space. Each source can keep all its snapshots, the last few, or a rolling set, and can run hourly, daily or weekly.
docs.library.p3: On Snapshots, Restore lets you browse a snapshot's files, choose a destination and decide what happens to files that already exist. Forget drops a snapshot, and Reclaim space frees the chunks nothing uses any more.
docs.salvage.p1: Salvage, in the footer, copies whatever can still be read of a file on a damaged drive. Choose the file, then where to write the copy.
docs.salvage.p2: Unreadable spots are retried in smaller and smaller pieces, then filled with zeros so the rest of the file keeps its place, and a map of the gaps is saved beside the copy. Run Salvage again on the same file later and only the gaps are tried.
docs.salvage.p3: A salvaged file with gaps is not a byte-exact copy, and its history entry says so.
docs.server.p1: Freally File Manager can serve a folder to other computers over WebDAV, plain HTTP, an S3-compatible API or SFTP.
docs.server.s1: Open Settings → Server and tick the protocols to offer.
docs.server.s2: Set the bind address. The default, 127.0.0.1:8080, serves only this computer; 0.0.0.0:8080 or your network address serves others, once your firewall allows it.
docs.server.s3: Choose the served folder, tick Read-only if nothing should be uploaded or deleted, and choose the authentication: none, a bearer token, or a user name and password.
docs.server.s4: Click Start server. The status line shows the address, and a Metrics link points to the Prometheus endpoint. Stop server, or quitting the app, stops it.
docs.server.webdav: Map a network drive in Windows, Connect to Server in Finder, GNOME Files or davfs2
docs.server.http: A web browser, curl or wget
docs.server.s3client: The AWS command line, rclone or any S3 library, with the user name and password as the access key and secret
docs.server.sftp: sftp, scp, FileZilla, WinSCP or rclone
docs.server.p2: WebDAV and HTTP can run together on one address; S3 and SFTP each need a server of their own, and S3 needs a password or no authentication rather than a token.
docs.server.p3: A server open to the network with no authentication can be read, and written unless it is read-only, by anything that can reach it. Beyond your own computer, always set a token or a password.
docs.server.p4: On a computer without a screen, the freally command does the same:
docs.migrate.p1: The freally migrate command reads another backup tool's repository, rebuilds every file and stores it in a repository in the open CDR-0 format, deduplicated again with Freally File Manager's own chunking.
docs.migrate.p2: Each importer is tested to restore every file byte for byte. The CDR-0 format is described in the specification published beside this site.
docs.settings.p1: The gear in the footer opens Settings. Changes take effect at once, with no restart. The tabs you will use most:
docs.settings.general: General: language, the app's theme, start at login, minimize to the tray, how errors are shown, the paste shortcut and the clipboard watcher.
docs.settings.transfer: Transfer: verification, buffer size, how many files copy at once, clones, timestamps and permissions, sparse files, locked files and the security marks a file carries.
docs.settings.filters: Filters: what to include and exclude.
docs.settings.shell: Shell: the right-click menu and taking over Windows' own copy.
docs.settings.network: Network: a speed limit, fixed or on a schedule.
docs.settings.updates: Updates: the daily update check, and a button to check now.
docs.settings.profiles: Profiles: save your settings under a name, switch between them, and import or export them.
docs.shortcuts.paste: Paste copied files through Freally File Manager, from anywhere
docs.shortcuts.undo: Undo the newest copy or move
docs.shortcuts.pause: Pause or resume the focused job
docs.shortcuts.escape: Close the topmost dialog or drawer
docs.trouble.slow.title: Why is my copy slow?
docs.trouble.slow.body: While a copy runs below the speed it should reach, the header shows a small badge naming the cause: the source disk, the destination disk, the network, an antivirus scanner, the processor or heat. Hover it for details.
docs.trouble.stall.title: A copy stops at 100%
docs.trouble.stall.body: If the header says Verifying, the copy is being checked against its checksum. That is normal for large files; switch verification off in Settings → Transfer if you do not need it.
docs.trouble.locked.title: A file is in use on Windows
docs.trouble.locked.body: Files are opened so that other programs can keep using them, and a refused file is retried a few times. If another program still holds it exclusively, close that program, or choose in Settings → Transfer to copy locked files from a snapshot.
docs.trouble.permission.title: Permission denied
docs.trouble.permission.body: When files are refused for permissions, Freally File Manager can retry them through one administrator prompt for the whole list, showing exactly which files it will touch before you approve.
docs.trouble.changed.title: Source changed during copy
docs.trouble.changed.body: The file changed while it was being read, so the copy may mix old and new contents. By default the file is flagged; Settings → Transfer can copy it again once or fail it instead.
docs.report.p1: When the app itself causes an error, a Report button appears beside the message. After a crash, the next launch offers Report or Dismiss.
docs.report.p2: Report opens this page in your browser, with the technical facts already filled in: you can read them but not change them. Add what you were doing and, if you like, an email address for a reply.
docs.report.p3: Nothing is sent unless you press Send on that page, and nothing is ever sent in the background. File paths in a report are shortened, with your home folder shown as ~.
docs.privacy.p1: Freally File Manager has no account and no telemetry. The telemetry switch in its settings is permanently off: a value written into the settings file by hand is ignored.
docs.privacy.p2: Copying, moving and verifying files on your own drives make no network requests. The app goes online for the things you set up, such as the file server or testing a cloud account, and to check for updates when it starts, at most once a day. The update check reads only the list of releases, sends none of your files or paths, and can be switched off in Settings → Updates.
docs.privacy.p3: It contains no AI: everything it decides comes from checksums, sizes and timestamps, and no machine-learning library is part of it.
search.none: Nothing on this site matches that.
